questions.q: Core: Label the drainage basin diagram and complete the upper, middle and lower course table.
Extend: Use an online map to trace the Thames and name three tributaries and their confluence towns.
questions.a: For example: Cherwell at Oxford, Kennet at Reading, Lea in London

questions.q: Stretch: Explain why the load gets smaller and rounder downstream.
questions.a: Attrition knocks stones together as they are carried, so they wear down

questions.q: Where two rivers meet is a:
questions.a: B) Confluence. A confluence is where a tributary joins a river.

questions.q: Big question: how does a river change on its journey?
questions.a: It gets wider, deeper and gentler, carries more water and smaller sediment
